spurt2_domain_findings.status: CONFIRMED against source by two independent reads (crew + lead). NOT YET IN SPEC.md.
spurt2_domain_findings.claim: 'Human approved' does not mean a human assented. ParseFiler writes a HUMAN approval on the user's behalf for any analysis in use in a segment.
spurt2_domain_findings.citation: FieldWorks/Src/LexText/ParserCore/ParseFiler.cs:302-320, SetUnsuccessfulParseEvals. Comment at :310 reads 'ensure that used analyses have a user evaluation'; :311 does m_userAgent.SetEvaluation(analysis, Opinions.approves) when the analysis (or one of its glosses) appears in wordform.OccurrencesBag segment analyses -- and it fires BEFORE the noopinion/delete check at :313-318.
spurt2_domain_findings.scope_correction: BROADER than first reported. SetUnsuccessfulParseEvals is called on BOTH result branches at ParseFiler.cs:231 (ErrorMessage != null) and :238 (successful parse), for every wordform whose Checksum changed. So this is not a failure-path quirk -- every filing run writes user approvals across all processed wordforms.
consequences: HumanApprovedAnalyses already contains analyses no human ever reviewed. It means 'a human approved this, OR it was in a text when the parser last ran.' Every G3 tier that reads human approval as human judgement is weaker than the spec assumes.
The single_probe_note is measuring the wrong thing: a user-noopinion count is NOT 'never human-reviewed', because in-segment analyses were silently upgraded out of noopinion.
Protective corollary for P0-1: in-segment analyses are shielded from the non-undoable delete. The deletion set is the conjunction 'user-noopinion AND not in any segment'.
spurt2_domain_findings.next_action: Spec edit in the G3 oracle section(s) + 12.3 deletion projection. Lead's call: this is a one-agent doc edit informed by a short domain pass, not a full cycle -- but it must land before any G3 tier text is treated as settled.

spurt2_domain_findings.claim: The HermitCrab agent is not created at project bootstrap, yet DefaultParserAgent looks it up by GUID and that lookup throws on a miss.
spurt2_domain_findings.citation: liblcm/src/SIL.LCModel/DomainServices/BootstrapNewLanguageProject.cs:140-165 (SetupAgents) creates exactly three agents -- kguidAgentDefUser, kguidAgentXAmpleParser, kguidAgentComputer -- and NOT kguidAgentHermitCrabParser. liblcm/src/SIL.LCModel/DomainImpl/OverridesLangProj.cs:218-231, LangProject.DefaultParserAgent, does ICmAgentRepository.GetObject(kguidAgentHermitCrabParser) when MorphologicalDataOA.ActiveParser == 'HC'. Its own XML doc comment at :216 declares <exception cref="KeyNotFoundException"/>, so the throw is documented behaviour, not speculation.
consequences: On a project that has never run HC, anything filing under the HC agent may throw KeyNotFoundException.
This interacts with the CP1 health block: an unhandled throw surfaces as a crash rather than a clean parser_* refusal. CP1's preflight should probe for the agent and refuse cleanly.
